info.name: Missivus
info.summary: Send Nextcloud email through Microsoft 365 without SMTP or a user login
info.description:
**Send all of Nextcloud's outgoing email — share notifications, password resets, activity digests, admin alerts — through Microsoft Graph using application permissions and one shared mailbox.**
Microsoft has retired basic-authentication SMTP for Microsoft 365, and Nextcloud's outgoing mail settings only speak SMTP or sendmail. The usual answers are an external relay daemon or a mailer that makes a person click "Connect" and then sends as that person. Missivus is neither: OAuth2 client credentials, the `Mail.Send` application permission, and an Exchange application access policy that locks the app to a single shared mailbox. No user account, no license for the mailbox, nothing to click, nothing that breaks when someone leaves.
- Replaces the system mailer for core **and** every app; installing it changes nothing until you switch it on - Client secret or certificate credentials; tokens cached in Nextcloud's distributed cache - From is always the configured shared mailbox (a differing requested sender is kept as Reply-To and logged) - Attachments up to Graph's inline ceiling and beyond it via upload sessions - Optional fallback to Nextcloud's own mailer, **off by default**; every failure is logged loudly, never swallowed - Admin settings with a test-email button, `config.php` overrides for every value, and `occ missivus:test` / `occ missivus:status`
**Privacy:** when enabled, this app connects to `login.microsoftonline.com` (to obtain access tokens) and `graph.microsoft.com` (to send mail). No other external service is contacted, and nothing is sent anywhere until you configure and enable it.
Missivus is free and open source (GPLv3). If you would rather not do the Entra and Exchange setup yourself, [Solvetus](https://solvetus.com) offers paid installation and support.
info.author: Solvetus
